message.content:
I just root-caused a bug on the Nxeon platform (Next.js app at /opt/nxeon, prod nginx config at /etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-cloud): the main `location /` block in that nginx vhost has NO proxy_read_timeout override, so it inherits nginx's default of 60 seconds. Some Server Actions in the app (e.g. lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts's createFreeMinecraftServer, which does an SSH+docker-run+wait-for-ready cycle that can legitimately take up to ~180s for plugin-heavy presets) run longer than that. When nginx hits the 60s ceiling it kills the wait for the upstream and serves /opt/nxeon/public/maintenance.html (via `error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;`) instead — the browser's React Server Components client can't parse that HTML as a Flight/RSC response, so it shows a generic "Something went wrong" crash to the user, even though the backend action is often still running (and may complete successfully moments later, orphaned from the user's view).

I'm about to fix the nginx timeout itself (raising proxy_read_timeout on that location block). Separately, I need you to find out: are there OTHER slow, real-provisioning server actions in this codebase that plausibly also exceed 60 seconds and would have been silently hitting this exact same nginx-timeout-into-broken-page bug? Specifically look at:
- lib/game-order.ts (paid game server orders — likely real VM/container provisioning via Proxmox or SSH)
- Any VPS/server deploy action (grep for "Deploy" under app/dashboard or lib/actions*.ts)
- Shared hosting provisioning
- Any other lib/actions-*.ts file that does withServerSsh / SSH exec calls with timeouts of 60s or more, or calls into Proxmox (qm create, qm start, etc.) which can genuinely take a while

For each one you find, note: the file/function, roughly how long it could plausibly take (look at any exec() timeout values passed, or comments describing expected duration), and whether it's reachable from a customer-facing Server Action (called from a form/page a real customer would hit) as opposed to purely an admin/internal action.

This is investigation only — do not edit any files. Report back concisely (a list, not prose) so I can decide whether this nginx timeout fix needs to be scoped more broadly or whether the single blanket fix to the main location block already covers everything (it likely does, since it's a location-level timeout, but I want to know the blast radius of what's been silently broken so I can decide whether to mention it to the user and whether anything else needs checking, like whether any of these flows have the SAME kind of DB-row-orphaning risk on timeout that free-mc had).

790	 * within seconds, and the customer's client still got "Failed to connect —
791	 * Timed out" because the server was still mid-boot. Polling the log line
792	 * itself is the only signal that means what it says.
793	 *
794	 * `docker restart` re-runs the exact same boot sequence as a fresh `docker
795	 * run`, so this same wait is needed after `applyModeProperties`'s restart
796	 * too, not just the initial container creation.
797	 */
798	async function waitForServerReady(
799	  conn: Client,
800	  containerName: string,
801	  // 110s covers a plain/properties-only boot with room to spare. A "plugins"
802	  // preset installs its Modrinth projects (download + Paper plugin-loader
803	  // init) BEFORE the JVM's own "Done (Xs)!" timer even starts counting, which
804	  // a live, reproduced customer failure showed can push total wall-clock time
805	  // past 110s even when the JVM's own boot only reports ~76s — this function
806	  // was giving up ~2s before a real, healthy SkyBlock server finished
807	  // starting, deleting its DB row while the container kept running, orphaned
808	  // (invisible to the customer, indefinitely occupying a capacity slot).
809	  // Callers pass FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS for any "plugins"-kind preset.
810	  timeoutMs = 110_000,
811	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
812	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
813	  // First few seconds are the container just starting up (image entrypoint,
814	  // ownership fix, etc.) — no point polling logs before that's underway.
815	  await sleep(3_000);
816	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
817	    const running = await exec(conn, `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`, 10_000);
818	    if (running.code !== 0 || running.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
819	      return { ok: false, error: "Container exited before finishing startup." };
820	    }
821	    const logs = await exec(conn, `docker logs ${shellQuote(containerName)} --tail 200 2>&1`, 10_000);
822	    if (/\bDone \([\d.]+s\)!/.test(logs.stdout)) return { ok: true };
823	    await sleep(3_000);
824	  }
825	  return { ok: false, error: "Server took too long to start." };
826	}

content.content:
851	export async function recreateGameTypeContainer(
852	  conn: Client,
853	  params: {
854	    containerName: string;
855	    dataPath: string;
856	    subdomain: string;
857	    domain: string;
858	    ramMb: number;
859	    ownerId: string;
860	    gameType: FreeMcGameType;
861	    gameTypeKey: string;
862	    gameMode: FreeMcGameMode;
863	    /** Extra env vars layered on top of the type's own (e.g. the Mod Menu's
864	     *  merged MODRINTH_PROJECTS list) — last-write-wins over the type's env. */
865	    extraEnv?: Record<string, string>;
866	  },
867	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
868	  const jvmRatio = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 0.7 : 0.85; // plugins need more non-heap headroom — see FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION's neighboring history
869	  const cpus = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 2 : 1; // see recreatePresetContainer's note on mc-router's fixed 60s wake timeout
870	  // The global free_minecraft_ram_mb setting (1024 by default) is sized for
871	  // the properties-only presets — plugins-kind ones (EssentialsX + LuckPerms
872	  // + Vault + a type's own plugins, up to 6 loaded dimensions on something
873	  // like SkyBlock) run noticeably heavier and were found live to OOM-kill a
874	  // short while AFTER printing "Done" at that ceiling — not during boot, so
875	  // the old shallow "still alive 15s after docker run" check never caught it,
876	  // and the fix wasn't the plugins themselves (confirmed by re-testing with
877	  // WorldEdit removed — same crash, same timing) or --cpus. It really is a
878	  // sizing problem: 1536m/0.7 ran the same SkyBlock config stable for 100s+
879	  // post-boot with ONE player — but confirmed live it's still not enough
880	  // once a SECOND player joins: memory climbed to 90% (1.355GB/1.5GB) during
881	  // the second player's own island-creation schematic paste (world-gen +
882	  // chunk load + plugin bookkeeping for two islands across up to 6
883	  // dimensions at once), and the container was killed twice in that window
884	  // before settling. 2560m/0.7 gives real headroom for that case; the free
885	  // tier is a shared/social product, so "two friends on one server" is the
886	  // common case, not an edge case. Bump container memory for plugin-kind
887	  // presets specifically rather than raising the global default (which
888	  // properties-only presets don't need).
889	  const ramMb = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? Math.max(params.ramMb, 2560) : params.ramMb;
890	  const jvmMb = Math.max(256, Math.round(ramMb * jvmRatio));
891	
892	  const envVars = { ...envForGameType(params.gameType), ...(params.extraEnv ?? {}), LEVEL: params.gameTypeKey };
893	  const envFlags = Object.entries(envVars)
894	    .map(([k, v]) => `-e ${k}=${shellQuote(v)}`)
895	    .join(" ");
896	
897	  // Removed FIRST, checked SECOND: if this account's own container was
898	  // already running, `docker rm -f` frees its committed cpus/ramMb before the
899	  // capacity snapshot below is taken, so this account's own prior usage never
900	  // counts against itself (a type switch that keeps the SAME cpu/ram class,
901	  // e.g. plugins->plugins, must never get blocked by its own old container).
902	  // This is also why every docker-run-issuing caller (create, type switch,
903	  // subdomain change, the legacy preset switch) gets this check for free
904	  // without needing its own copy — see lib/freemc-capacity.ts's module doc
905	  // for why this is gated at all and why the passive mc-router wake path
906	  // deliberately is NOT.
907	  await exec(conn, `docker rm -f ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`, 30_000);
908	
909	  const capacity = await getFreemcHostCapacity(conn);
910	  const capCheck = wouldExceedFreemcCapacity(capacity, cpus, ramMb);
911	  if (capCheck.exceeds) {
912	    return { ok: false, error: "Free servers are at capacity right now — try again in a few minutes." };
913	  }
914	
915	  const cmd = [
916	    "docker run -d",
917	    `--name ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`,
918	    "--network freemc",
919	    `--memory=${ramMb}m --memory-swap=${ramMb}m --cpus=${cpus}`,
920	    `--label mc-router.host=${shellQuote(`${params.subdomain}.${params.domain}`)}`,
921	    `-v ${shellQuote(params.dataPath)}:/data`,
922	    `-e EULA=TRUE -e TYPE=${params.gameType.type ?? "VANILLA"} -e ONLINE_MODE=FALSE`,
923	    params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? `-e VERSION=${shellQuote(FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION)}` : "",
924	    `-e MEMORY=${jvmMb}m`,
925	    `-e ENABLE_RCON=true -e RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(rconPasswordFor(params.ownerId))}`,
926	    envFlags,
927	    "itzg/minecraft-server",
928	  ].join(" ");
929	  const run = await exec(conn, cmd, 90_000); // plugin downloads can take longer than a plain boot
930	  if (run.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: run.stderr || "docker run failed" };
931	
932	  const ready = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName, params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS : undefined);
933	  if (!ready.ok) return ready;
934	
935	  // IridiumSkyblock ships with `islandCreateOnJoin: false` — a customer who
936	  // joins fresh just spawns in the plain overworld terrain (which, since
937	  // that's Paper's stock generator, looks exactly like Vanilla), with no
938	  // floating island and no indication one exists to create. Confirmed live:
939	  // a customer reported "joined the server but it has vanilla loaded even
940	  // though I chose skyblock" — this is why. The config file only exists
941	  // after the plugin's first boot (it writes its own defaults), so this has
942	  // to run as a post-boot patch, not something bakeable into the image/env.
943	  // Patched HERE — right after the first readiness wait, BEFORE
944	  // applyModeProperties's own restart below — so that ONE restart picks up
945	  // both this and the mode properties together. An earlier version patched
946	  // this AFTER applyModeProperties with its own separate restart+wait, which
947	  // meant a SkyBlock switch chained three full boot-and-wait cycles back to
948	  // back (each 40-90s) — confirmed live to run past whatever the browser/
949	  // client was willing to wait for, so the switch would actually succeed
950	  // server-side a couple minutes later while the customer had already seen
951	  // a timeout/error and given up. Two cycles instead of three meaningfully
952	  // shortens that window; a config patch with no plugin process running yet
953	  // to pick it up costs nothing extra by itself.
954	  //
955	  // `islandCreateOnJoin` alone was not the whole bug: it only makes the
956	  // plugin create the island in the background. Whether the player actually
957	  // gets TELEPORTED there is a separate key, `spawnOnIsland`, which also
958	  // ships `false` — so even with an island silently created, the player was
959	  // left standing in that same plain default-generator "skyblock" level,
960	  // which is exactly the "shows active on skyblock but loads vanilla world"
961	  // report. Both keys have to be true for a fresh join to actually land the
962	  // player on their island.
963	  //
964	  // `paster: "worldedit"` is a third default-config landmine: this server
965	  // stack never installs WorldEdit (the boot log warns "selected paster
966	  // [worldedit] is not available, available choices are [internalAsync]"),
967	  // and running `/is create` against that misconfiguration killed the whole
968	  // Minecraft process outright — instant death, no Java exception, no JVM
969	  // crash dump, exit code -1 from mc-server-runner. Confirmed live: with
970	  // `paster: "internalAsync"` (the only paster actually available) patched
971	  // in, `/is create` completes normally. internalAsync is the plugin's own
972	  // built-in pasting implementation and needs no other plugin installed.
973	  if (params.gameTypeKey === "skyblock") {
974	    const patch = await exec(
975	      conn,
976	      `docker exec ${shellQuote(params.containerName)} sed -i ` +
977	        `-e 's/islandCreateOnJoin: false/islandCreateOnJoin: true/' ` +
978	        `-e 's/spawnOnIsland: false/spawnOnIsland: true/' ` +
979	        `-e 's/paster: "worldedit"/paster: "internalAsync"/' ` +
980	        `/data/plugins/IridiumSkyblock/configuration.yml`,
981	      10_000,
982	    );
983	    if (patch.code !== 0) {
984	      console.error("[free-minecraft] SkyBlock island-spawn config patch failed (non-fatal):", patch.stderr);
985	    }
986	  }
987	
988	  // Prison ships with ZERO mines out of the box — confirmed live (2026-08-25),
989	  // same investigation session as the SkyBlock fix above. A fresh customer
990	  // selecting Prison landed in plain default-generator terrain with no rank,
991	  // no mine, no indication the plugin was even active — the exact same "looks
992	  // like vanilla" report, but for a different root cause: Prison's Ranks
993	  // module was silently failing to enable at all ("No Economy Plugin Active"
994	  // in the boot log) because nothing in its env provided Vault + an economy
995	  // plugin. Fixed by adding vaultunlocked+essentialsx to prison's
996	  // MODRINTH_PROJECTS above (same pairing skyblock/towny already use) — boot
997	  // log then shows "Module: Ranks : Enabled" with "EssentialsX Economy
998	  // (Vault) <Active>".
999	  //
1000	  // That alone still isn't enough: Prison has no default mine either. Its own
1001	  // `/ranks autoConfigure` command (console-safe — its @Command annotation is
1002	  // `onlyPlayers = false`) auto-creates 26 ranks (A-Z) AND 26 matching virtual
1003	  // mines with blocks already assigned and linked to their ranks — confirmed
1004	  // live via RCON (`mines list ALL` showed all 26 as "Virtual Mine" right
1005	  // after running this). Run it here, post-boot, same slot as the SkyBlock
1006	  // patch, so it's picked up before the container's already-scheduled
1007	  // mode-properties restart rather than costing a THIRD boot cycle.
1008	  //
1009	  // It does NOT get all the way to playable: Prison's own mine-placement
1010	  // command (`/mines set area <name> feet`) calls `sender.getPlatformPlayer()`
1011	  // unconditionally (confirmed by reading MinesCommands.java's
1012	  // `redefineCommand`), so it can only run as an actual player standing
1013	  // somewhere in the world — there is no console/RCON equivalent, and no
1014	  // fixed coordinate is safe to fake blind (mirrors the wall SkyBlock's
1015	  // `paster: "worldedit"` fix avoided by not depending on WorldEdit at all).
1016	  // That one remaining step is covered by prison's setupNote instead of being
1017	  // silently left broken.
1018	  if (params.gameTypeKey === "prison") {
1019	    const autoConfig = await sendRcon(conn, params.containerName, params.ownerId, "ranks autoConfigure");
1020	    if (!autoConfig.ok) {
1021	      console.error("[free-minecraft] Prison ranks/mines auto-configure failed (non-fatal):", autoConfig.error);
1022	    }
1023	  }
1024	
1025	  // Branded Nxeon join message + this game type's own command hints (see
1026	  // "let players be aware of the island commands... for other game types" —
1027	  // the 2026-08-25 welcome-message feature). Every kind:"plugins" type now
1028	  // installs EssentialsX (see each preset's env above), so this patch is
1029	  // universal across all 8 of them — same timing as the SkyBlock patch just
1030	  // above, right after the first readiness wait and before the mode-restart
1031	  // below, so ONE restart picks up everything. kind:"properties" (currently
1032	  // just vanilla) has no plugin runtime at all — TYPE=VANILLA can't load
1033	  // Bukkit plugins — so it's intentionally NOT covered here; there's no
1034	  // config-file-only, version-safe way to get a join broadcast onto a plain
1035	  // vanilla server without either flipping it onto Paper (a real
1036	  // architecture change, out of scope for a join-message feature) or a
1037	  // datapack pinned to a specific pack_format (which vanilla deliberately
1038	  // avoids by tracking itzg's LATEST — see FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION's
1039	  // neighboring history for exactly the kind of breakage that invites).
1040	  if (params.gameType.kind === "plugins") {
1041	    const welcomeMessage = buildFreemcWelcomeMessage(params.gameType);
1042	    const patch = await patchEssentialsJoinMessage(conn, params.containerName, welcomeMessage);
1043	    if (!patch.ok) {
1044	      console.error("[free-minecraft] Welcome-message config patch failed (non-fatal):", patch.error);
1045	    }
1046	  }
1047	
1048	  const modeApplied = await applyModeProperties(conn, params.containerName, params.ownerId, params.gameMode);
1049	  if (!modeApplied.ok) return { ok: false, error: modeApplied.error || "Could not apply the active game mode." };
1050	
1051	  // applyModeProperties ends in a `docker restart`, which re-runs the exact
1052	  // same boot sequence as the `docker run` above — needs the same real
1053	  // readiness wait, not a fixed few-second sleep. This restart is also what
1054	  // picks up the SkyBlock config patch above, if it ran.
1055	  const readyAfterMode = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName, params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS : undefined);
1056	  if (!readyAfterMode.ok) {
1057	    return { ok: false, error: readyAfterMode.error || "Server didn't come back up after applying the active game mode." };
1058	  }
1059	
1060	  return { ok: true };
1061	}

content.text:
## Investigation Results — nginx 60s timeout blast radius

**Architecture note first (this shapes everything below):** most "provisioning" work in this codebase is dispatched via a `db.job.create({ type: "PROVISION"/"WEBSITE_CREATE"/"DB_CREATE"/"APP_INSTALL"/etc })` (or `hostingTask.create`) row inside a fast DB transaction, then picked up by the separate `worker` process — *not* run inline on the Server Action's request thread. Those are **not** vulnerable to this bug at all, because the HTTP response returns in milliseconds regardless of how long the actual work takes. Confirmed this pattern for:
- `lib/game-order.ts` `placeGameOrder` — paid game server orders. Just debits wallet, creates invoice, `tx.job.create({type:"PROVISION"})`, returns. No SSH/Proxmox call on the request thread.
- `lib/order.ts` `placeOrder` — paid VPS orders, same pattern (`lib/order.ts:979`).
- `lib/actions-websites.ts`, `lib/actions-databases.ts`, `lib/actions-apps.ts` — all `db.job.create`, real work in `worker/websites.ts` / `worker/databases.ts` / `worker/apps.ts` (which is where `INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15 min lives).
- `lib/actions-hosting.ts` (shared hosting) — everything routes through `db.hostingTask.create` (APP_INSTALL, PHP_SWITCH, BACKUP, RESTORE, CREATE_SUBDOMAIN, etc.), not inline SSH.
- `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`, `actions-volumes.ts`, `actions-firewall.ts`, `actions-ssl.ts`, `actions-sites.ts` — same job-queue pattern.
- `lib/actions-migrate.ts`'s actual migration engine — job-queued (`db.job.create` at line 679); only lightweight read-only probes (`QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS`=12s) run inline.

So `game-order.ts` and the VPS order path are **not** part of the blast radius — good news there.

### Genuinely at-risk: customer-facing, synchronous, long-running SSH inside the Server Action

**1. `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` `recreateGameTypeContainer()` (shared helper) — still plausibly exceeds even the just-applied 300s fix**
   - Chain per call: `docker rm -f` (30s cap) → `docker run` (90s cap) → `waitForServerReady()` **up to 180s** (`FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`, `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts:229`) → skyblock/prison config patches (~10s) → `applyModeProperties` (RCON + `docker restart`, 30s cap) → **second** `waitForServerReady()` up to another 180s.
   - Configured worst case for a *single, non-rollback* call is ~520s of timeout headroom (two 180s waits alone = 360s) — already past the 300s `proxy_read_timeout` that's now live in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-cloud`.
   - Reached from these **customer-facing** (`requireUser()`, not admin) Server Actions, all of which call it **twice** on failure (forward attempt + rollback-to-previous-type), roughly doubling worst case:
     - `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` `applyFreeMinecraftPreset` (~line 552)
     - `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` `switchFreeMinecraftGameType` (~line 101)
     - `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts` `applyFreeMinecraftMods` (~line 49)
   - Same class of bug as `createFreeMinecraftServer`, just with an even higher configured ceiling. Worth checking whether 300s is actually enough here, or whether these three call sites need a longer location-specific override (or need to move to the job-queue pattern like everything else).
   - Orphan-risk difference vs. `createFreeMinecraftServer`: no *resource* orphan (on failure it explicitly rolls back to the previous container rather than deleting the DB row), but the same "customer sees maintenance.html/crash, backend keeps running and DB gets updated moments later to the correct end state" false-failure UX applies — a customer who sees the error and retries could race their own in-flight recreate.

**2. `lib/actions-migrate.ts` `finishMigrationSetup()` (~line 1252) — customer-facing, NOT job-queued, likely still at risk after the fix**
   - Reachable by a regular customer for their own migration (`ownedMigrationForRemediation`: `m.userId !== user.id && user.role !== "ADMIN"` gate, so it's not admin-only).
   - Loops over up to 20 compose directories, running `docker compose up -d` inline with a **300,000ms (300s) timeout per directory** (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:1282`), then a systemd unit-start loop (60s), an nginx reload (30s), a 12s sleep, then a final re-probe SSH round-trip.
   - Even one compose stack running near its own 300s ceiling already meets/exceeds the current nginx `proxy_read_timeout 300s`; with 2+ slow stacks this comfortably blows past it. This is the strongest remaining candidate for "still broken after the fix you just shipped."

**3. `lib/actions-claude-backfill.ts` (admin/fleet-only, lower priority but worth knowing)**
   - `backfillServerClaude` → `lib/claude-backfill.ts` `backfillClaudeCli` runs an install script with `INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15 minutes (`lib/ssh-exec.ts:38`, env-overridable) inline over SSH — not job-queued.
   - Gated by `requireArea("fleet")`, i.e. staff/admin only, and served on `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` (`nxeon-admin-cloud` vhost) — which I confirmed **already has** `proxy_read_timeout 300s;` on its `location /` (someone put the same override there). 300s is still far short of the 900s the install can legitimately take, so this admin flow can also hit the maintenance-page bug — just with staff as the blast radius, not customers.
   - `backfillAllServersClaude(limit=25)` compounds this further: it runs up to 25 servers **serially in one request**, so worst case is `25 × up to 900s` in a single Server Action call — this one is worth fixing regardless of the nginx timeout (e.g. background it), since no nginx timeout short of extreme values would cover it.

### On the nginx config itself
For what it's worth, the fix already appears to be live on disk: `/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-cloud`'s `location /` now has `proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` with a comment dated "Confirmed live 2026-09-02" — so either you already applied it or something else did. Sibling vhosts (`nxeon-staging`, `nxeon-staff`, `nxeon-admin-cloud`) already carry the same `300s` override; only `nxeon-mail`/`nxeon-staging` websocket-style locations use `3600s`. None of the vhosts currently set anything ≥ 520s, which is the actual configured ceiling for item #1 above.

### Bottom line for scoping the fix
- The blanket `location /` timeout raise is the right *shape* of fix and covers `createFreeMinecraftServer` and the vast majority of the app (since most heavy work is job-queued).
- It likely does **not** fully cover: the free-mc game-type/mods/preset-switch trio (`applyFreeMinecraftPreset`, `switchFreeMinecraftGameType`, `applyFreeMinecraftMods`) or `finishMigrationSetup` — all customer-facing, all synchronous, all with configured ceilings at or above the 300s you just set. Worth either raising the timeout further for `location /` specifically, or (better long-term) moving these onto the same job-queue pattern the rest of the provisioning code already uses, given the comments in `free-minecraft-control.ts` show this exact "silently succeeds after the customer already saw a timeout" failure mode has been hit and worked around before at the 110s/180s boundary.
